verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a roughly 10-day crewed test flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon" (R1); "10-day mission" (R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the mission is a ~10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Live updates from April 1, 2026 launch (R1); "Artemis II mission’s April 1 launch date" (R2); "slated to launch as early as April 1" (R3); "as soon as April 1" (R7); "April 1 is the first launch opportunity" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm launch on April 1, 2026, with R1 as live launch day blog.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is aimed at sending four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "send astronauts on a journey around the Moon" (R1); "journey around the moon" (R2); "send four astronauts around the moon" (R3, R5); similar in others
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the mission as sending four astronauts around the Moon and back.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission uses the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA’s Artemis II SLS rocket" (R1); "Space Launch System rocket" (R4, R5, R6, R7, R8)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes high-Earth orbit systems tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "high Earth orbit ahead of a proximity operations demonstration" (R1); "high, lopsided orbit" (R3); "high Earth elliptical orbit" (R5, R8); "high Earth orbit" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm initial phase in high Earth orbit for systems tests.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes a three-day outbound transit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "journey to the moon takes around three days" (R8); "Days 3–5: Journey toward the moon" (R5); next few days outbound (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as ~3 days outbound to Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes a lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lunar flyby" or "flyby" in all sources
verifications.reasoning: Core mission profile in every reference.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R3, R4, R5, R7, R8)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission tests the Orion spacecraft’s life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "test life-support systems" (R1); "validate the life-support" (R4); "test Orion's life-support system" (R5); "life-support" (R6)

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida"
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated in R1 launch blog.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is aimed for a 6:24 p.m. ET launch window.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "opening of today’s launch window is slated for just over 4 hours from now, at 6:24 p.m. EDT" (R1); "window between 6:24 p.m. ET and 8:24 p.m. ET" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match for launch window opening.

verifications.claim: After reaching orbit on Day 1 of the Artemis II mission, Orion separates from the upper stage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "core stage has successfully separated from the interim cryogenic propulsion stage and the Orion spacecraft" then upper stage ops (R1); "spaceship separates from the upper stage" (R5)

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of the Artemis II mission, the crew deploys solar arrays.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "6:59 p.m. The Orion spacecraft’s SAWs (solar arrays wings) have fully deployed" shortly after 6:35 p.m. launch

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of the Artemis II mission, the crew performs a 90-minute check of systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Orion will spend 90-minutes in its initial orbit"
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for Day 1 systems check.

verifications.claim: On Days 1-2 of the Artemis II mission, Orion spends about a day in a high-Earth elliptical orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Orion and the crew will spend about a day in high Earth orbit"

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes a proximity operations demonstration where crew members manually fly the craft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "proximity operations demonstration. This demonstration will test the ability to manually maneuver Orion" (R1); "steering their Orion capsule around it" (R3); similar in R5, R7

verifications.claim: On Day 2 of the Artemis II mission, Orion's service module fires to send the spacecraft toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Day 2: ... Orion's main engine will fire for ... translunar injection" (R5); "Days 2 - 4: Outbound transit ... translunar injection burn" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: TLI burn on Day 2 to head to Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission sets Orion on a figure-eight, free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "large figure-eight trajectory" (R4); "figure-eight flight path ... lunar free-return trajectory" (R8)

verifications.claim: On Days 2-4 of the Artemis II mission, Orion spends roughly three days traveling to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Days 2 - 4: Outbound transit A journey to the moon takes around three days."

verifications.claim: On Days 5-6 of the Artemis II mission, the crew swings around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Day 6: Lunar flyby" (R5); "Day 5 - 6: Lunar fly-by" (R8)

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II lunar flyby, the crew passes thousands of miles beyond the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "several thousand miles beyond the moon" (R3); "thousands of miles beyond the Moon’s far side" (R4); "4,000 and 6,000 miles" (R5, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Specific distances in thousands of miles.

verifications.claim: On Days 7-10 of the Artemis II mission, the spacecraft returns to Earth relying on Earth's gravity to guide its path back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Days 7–9: Heading back home ... rely on the combined gravity"
verifications.reasoning: Free-return uses gravity for return, aligns with days.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of the Artemis II mission, Orion reenters the atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Day 10: Reentry" (R5); reentry on Day 10 (R7)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission tests the heat shield during reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "All eyes will be on Orion's heat shield" (R3); "critical tests will involve Orion’s heat shield" (R4); heat shield test (R6)

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of the Artemis II mission, Orion splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Day 10: Reentry and crew recovery ... splashdown"

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch (Mission Specialist), and Jeremy Hansen (Mission Specialist).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Exact crew and roles listed consistently (e.g., R1, R2, etc.)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II spacecraft is the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Orion spacecraft" throughout all sources

verifications.claim: The objective of the Artemis II mission is to validate life-support systems and verify crew performance in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "validate life-support systems" (R4); "verify that its life-support ... work as designed in deep space" (R5); "test life-support ... in deep space" (R6)
